correctness.rationale: For all n>=1 every swap edge lies in exactly one triangle: swap-only parity excludes 3 swaps, Hamming weight excludes 2 swaps, and replacement parity excludes zero swaps. The one-triangle-per-swap correspondence is exact. For any Eulerian replacement-edge set, eliminating paired down-edges at a maximal-weight vertex using a replacement square strictly reduces an integer potential, proving square generation in all dimensions. The resulting T triangles plus B independent Hamming squares span and are linearly independent by private swap coordinates and replacement-square rank. The universal cycle-basis lower bound is 3T+4B; its equality conditions force all T triangles and only 4-cycles besides them. Fibonacci convolutions derive H,T and L. Finite implementation checks all premises for n=1,...,11, including GF(2) cycle-rank equality; it is not used to infer the infinite statement.

value.rationale: Minimum cycle bases are natural all-length graph-network invariants with real graph-algorithmic utility. The result completely determines the optimal cycle-basis weight of the tilde-Fibonacci family, identifies every swap triangle as compulsory in every optimum, and provides an explicit constructive algorithm using only local three- and four-edge loops. This is not a new parametrization of known vertex or edge counts: the forcing property concerns the internal structure of every optimal basis. The exact scope is unweighted binary swap/mismatch networks; the finding does not claim a general or downstream theorem.
